newsitem.title: USA: Central and South West sees rate cut order.
newsitem.headline: Central and South West sees rate cut order.

text.p: Central and South West Corp said it expected the Public Utility Commission of Texas to order an annual rate decrease ranging from $20 million to $30 million for its Central Power and Light Co on March 31.
The commission was also expected to order additional annual rate decreases of about $17 million in 1998 and 1999, the company said.
While the final amount of the rate decrease has not yet been calculated by the commission staff, it indicated it had decided most unresolved issues, the company said.
Commissioners were expected to designate approximately $859 million of invested capital associated with the South Texas Project nuclear generation plant as excess cost over market, the company said.

If it rules as expected, Centra Power's excess cost over market could receive a 7.96 percent return on equity as compared with the 10.9 percent return approved for all other invested capital, the company said.

Excess cost over market refers to the amount of costs that potentially would become "stranded" if retail competition were mandated and prices were set in the market, rather than when the cost of investment determined by current regulatory standards of prudent investment costs, it said.
